title: Visual Block
intro: `Ctrl-v` selects a rectangle, a column of text across several lines. `d` deletes the column and `c` replaces it on every line. `I` inserts text before the block on every line and `A` appends after it; use `$` first to append at each line's end, even when the lines are different lengths. The change shows on all lines when you press `Esc`.
summary: Edit a column of lines at once with Ctrl-v.

exercises.instruction: Comment out all three lines: `Ctrl-v`, `j` `j` to extend down, then `I`, type `// ` and press `Esc`.
hints: `I` in a block inserts at the left edge of every selected line.

exercises.instruction: Remove the numbering: `Ctrl-v`, `j` `j`, `l` `l` to cover `1. `, then `d`.
hints: The block is three columns wide and three lines tall.

exercises.instruction: Add a semicolon to the end of each line: `Ctrl-v`, `j` `j`, `$`, then `A;` and `Esc`.
hints: `$` stretches the block to each line's own end, so ragged lines work.

exercises.instruction: Turn every `var` into `let`: `Ctrl-v`, `j` `j`, `l` `l` to select `var`, then `c`, type `let` and `Esc`.
exercises.initialCode:
var a
var b
var c

goal.buffer:
let a
let b
let c

hints: `c` deletes the block and types your text on each line.

exercises.instruction: Turn the three lines into a Markdown list by putting `- ` in front of each.
Delete the `x` column from all three lines.
